tname: Distance and midpoints in 3D; volume and surface area of 3D solids; angles
text:
The points $A(1,\ -2,\ 3)$ and $B(5,\ k,\ -1)$ are such that $AB = 6$.

(a) Find the possible values of $k$. [3]

(b) Given that $k > -3$, find the coordinates of the midpoint of $[AB]$. [2]

tname: Distance and midpoints in 3D; volume and surface area of 3D solids; angles
text:
![right circular cone with base radius 5 cm and slant height 13 cm](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.1_2.svg)

The diagram shows a right circular cone with vertex $V$ and base centre $O$. The radius of the base is $5\text{ cm}$ and the slant height is $13\text{ cm}$. The vertical height of the cone is $h\text{ cm}$.

(a) Show that $h = 12$. [2]

(b) Find the volume of the cone. [2]

(c) Find the total surface area of the cone, including its base. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$h^2+5^2=13^2$ (M1)

$h=\sqrt{169-25}=\sqrt{144}$ A1

$h=12$ AG

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$V=\frac{1}{3}\pi(5^2)(12)$ (M1)

$=100\pi=314\text{ cm}^3$ $(314.159\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

curved surface area $=\pi(5)(13)=65\pi$ (A1)

base area $=25\pi$ (A1)

total $=90\pi=283\text{ cm}^2$ $(282.743\ldots)$ A1

Note: award (A1)(A0)A0 for $204\text{ cm}^2$ (curved surface only) if working is shown.

**[3 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: Distance and midpoints in 3D; volume and surface area of 3D solids; angles
text:
![cuboid ABCDEFGH with AB = 8 cm, BC = 6 cm, CG = 5 cm](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.1_3.svg)

The diagram shows a cuboid $ABCDEFGH$ with $AB = 8\text{ cm}$, $BC = 6\text{ cm}$ and $CG = 5\text{ cm}$.

(a) Find the length of the diagonal $AC$. [2]

(b) Find the length of the diagonal $AG$. [2]

(c) Find the angle between $[AG]$ and the base $ABCD$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$AC=\sqrt{8^2+6^2}$ (M1)

$=10\text{ cm}$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$AG=\sqrt{10^2+5^2}$ (or $\sqrt{8^2+6^2+5^2}$) (M1)

$=\sqrt{125}=11.2\text{ cm}$ $(11.1803\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

recognizing the required angle is $G\hat{A}C$, e.g. $\tan G\hat{A}C=\frac{5}{10}$ (M1)

$G\hat{A}C=26.6^\circ$ $(26.5650\ldots)$ A1

Note: accept $0.464$ radians. FT from their values in (a) or (b).

**[2 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Distance and midpoints in 3D; volume and surface area of 3D solids; angles
text:
![right pyramid VABCD on a square base of side 10 cm, height 12 cm](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.1_4.svg)

A solid right pyramid $VABCD$ has a square base $ABCD$ of side $10\text{ cm}$. The vertex $V$ is vertically above $M$, the centre of the base, and $VM = 12\text{ cm}$.

(a) Find the volume of the pyramid. [2]

(b) Let $N$ be the midpoint of $[AB]$. Show that $VN = 13\text{ cm}$. [2]

(c) Hence find the total surface area of the pyramid. [3]

(d) Find the angle between the edge $[VA]$ and the base $ABCD$. [4]

The pyramid is melted down and all of the material is used to make a solid sphere.

(e) Find the radius of the sphere. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$V=\frac{1}{3}(10^2)(12)$ (M1)

$=400\text{ cm}^3$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$MN=5$ (A1)

$VN=\sqrt{12^2+5^2}=\sqrt{169}$ A1

$=13$ AG

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

area of one triangular face $=\frac{1}{2}(10)(13)=65$ (A1)

total $=100+4(65)$ (M1)

$=360\text{ cm}^2$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(d)**

$MA=\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{10^2+10^2}=5\sqrt{2}\ (=7.07106\ldots)$ (M1)A1

$\tan V\hat{A}M=\frac{12}{5\sqrt{2}}$ (or $\sin V\hat{A}M=\frac{12}{\sqrt{194}}$, $VA=13.9284\ldots$) (M1)

$V\hat{A}M=59.5^\circ$ $(59.4910\ldots)$ A1

Note: accept $1.04$ radians.

**[4 marks]**

**(e)**

$\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3=400$ (M1)

$r^3=\frac{300}{\pi}=95.4929\ldots$ (A1)

$r=4.57\text{ cm}$ $(4.57078\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from their answer to (a).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [14 marks]**

tname: Distance and midpoints in 3D; volume and surface area of 3D solids; angles
text:
![solid made from a cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm with a hemisphere on top](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.1_5.svg)

A solid is made from a cylinder of radius $3\text{ cm}$ and height $10\text{ cm}$, with a hemisphere of radius $3\text{ cm}$ joined to its top face, as shown in the diagram.

(a) Find the volume of the solid. [3]

(b) Find the total surface area of the solid. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

cylinder: $\pi(3^2)(10)=90\pi$; hemisphere: $\frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{4}{3}\pi(3^3)=18\pi$ (A1)(A1)

volume $=108\pi=339\text{ cm}^3$ $(339.292\ldots)$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

base $9\pi$, curved surface of cylinder $2\pi(3)(10)=60\pi$, curved surface of hemisphere $\frac{1}{2}\cdot4\pi(3^2)=18\pi$ (A1)(A1)

Note: award (A1) for any two correct, (A1)(A1) for all three correct.

total $=87\pi=273\text{ cm}^2$ $(273.318\ldots)$ A1

Note: do not award the final A1 if the top face of the cylinder ($9\pi$) is included, giving $96\pi=302\text{ cm}^2$.

**[3 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangle trigonometry: sine rule, cosine rule, area
text:
![triangle ABC with AB = 5 cm, AC = 8 cm and angle A = 60 degrees](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.2_6.svg)

In triangle $ABC$, $AB = 5\text{ cm}$, $AC = 8\text{ cm}$ and $B\hat{A}C = 60^\circ$.

(a) Find $BC$. [3]

(b) Find the exact area of triangle $ABC$. [2]

tname: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangle trigonometry: sine rule, cosine rule, area
text:
![right-angled triangle PQR with right angle at Q, PQ = 7.2 cm and angle P = 38 degrees](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.2_7.svg)

In the triangle $PQR$, $P\hat{Q}R = 90^\circ$, $PQ = 7.2\text{ cm}$ and $Q\hat{P}R = 38^\circ$.

(a) Find $QR$. [2]

(b) Find $PR$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$\tan38^\circ=\frac{QR}{7.2}$ (M1)

$QR=5.63\text{ cm}$ $(5.62525\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$\cos38^\circ=\frac{7.2}{PR}$ (or Pythagoras with their $QR$) (M1)

$PR=9.14\text{ cm}$ $(9.13693\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (a) if Pythagoras is used.

**[2 marks]**

**Total [4 marks]**

tname: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangle trigonometry: sine rule, cosine rule, area
text:
![triangle ABC with AB = 11 cm, angle B = 42 degrees and angle C = 73 degrees](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.2_8.svg)

In triangle $ABC$, $AB = 11\text{ cm}$, $A\hat{B}C = 42^\circ$ and $A\hat{C}B = 73^\circ$.

(a) Find $AC$. [3]

(b) Find the area of triangle $ABC$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$\frac{AC}{\sin42^\circ}=\frac{11}{\sin73^\circ}$ (M1)A1

$AC=7.70\text{ cm}$ $(7.69674\ldots)$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$B\hat{A}C=180^\circ-42^\circ-73^\circ=65^\circ$ (A1)

area $=\frac{1}{2}(11)(7.69674\ldots)\sin65^\circ$ (M1)

$=38.4\text{ cm}^2$ $(38.3659\ldots)$ A1

Note: other valid methods, e.g. finding $BC=10.4249\ldots$ and using $\frac{1}{2}(11)(BC)\sin42^\circ$, receive full credit. FT from (a).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangle trigonometry: sine rule, cosine rule, area
text:
A triangular plot of land $PQR$ has sides $PQ = 7\text{ m}$, $QR = 9\text{ m}$ and $PR = 13\text{ m}$.

(a) Find the size of the largest angle of the triangle. [3]

(b) Find the area of the plot. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

largest angle is opposite the longest side, $P\hat{Q}R$ (R1)

$\cos P\hat{Q}R=\frac{7^2+9^2-13^2}{2(7)(9)}\ \left(=-\frac{39}{126}\right)$ M1

$P\hat{Q}R=108^\circ$ $(108.030\ldots)$ A1

Note: accept $1.89$ radians.

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

area $=\frac{1}{2}(7)(9)\sin108.030\ldots^\circ$ (M1)

$=30.0\text{ m}^2$ $(29.9530\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (a). Accept use of Heron's formula.

**[2 marks]**

**Total [5 marks]**

tname: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangle trigonometry: sine rule, cosine rule, area
text:
![quadrilateral ABCD with AB = 6 cm, BC = 9 cm, CD = 8 cm, DA = 7 cm, angle ABC = 110 degrees and diagonal AC](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.2_10.svg)

The diagram shows a quadrilateral $ABCD$ with $AB = 6\text{ cm}$, $BC = 9\text{ cm}$, $CD = 8\text{ cm}$, $DA = 7\text{ cm}$ and $A\hat{B}C = 110^\circ$.

(a) Find $AC$. [3]

(b) Find $B\hat{A}C$. [3]

(c) Find $A\hat{D}C$. [3]

(d) Find the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$. [4]
ms:
**(a)**

$AC^2=6^2+9^2-2(6)(9)\cos110^\circ$ (M1)

$AC^2=153.938\ldots$ (A1)

$AC=12.4\text{ cm}$ $(12.4071\ldots)$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$\frac{\sin B\hat{A}C}{9}=\frac{\sin110^\circ}{12.4071\ldots}$ (M1)A1

$B\hat{A}C=43.0^\circ$ $(42.9719\ldots)$ A1

Note: accept use of the cosine rule. FT from (a).

**[3 marks]**

**(c)**

$\cos A\hat{D}C=\frac{7^2+8^2-AC^2}{2(7)(8)}\ \left(=\frac{113-153.938\ldots}{112}=-0.365\ldots\right)$ (M1)A1

$A\hat{D}C=111^\circ$ $(111.439\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[3 marks]**

**(d)**

area $ABC=\frac{1}{2}(6)(9)\sin110^\circ\ (=25.3717\ldots)$ (M1)(A1)

area $ACD=\frac{1}{2}(7)(8)\sin111.439\ldots^\circ\ (=26.0625\ldots)$ (A1)

total area $=51.4\text{ cm}^2$ $(51.4342\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (c). Use of a rounded angle $111^\circ$ gives $51.5$; accept.

**[4 marks]**

**Total [13 marks]**

tname: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangle trigonometry: sine rule, cosine rule, area
text:
In triangle $ABC$, $AB = 6\text{ cm}$, $AC = 8\text{ cm}$ and $B\hat{A}C = \theta$. The area of the triangle is $12\text{ cm}^2$.

(a) Find the two possible values of $\theta$, giving your answers in radians. [3]

(b) Given that $\theta$ is obtuse, find $BC^2$, giving your answer in the form $a + b\sqrt{3}$ where $a,\ b\in\mathbb{Z}$. [3]

tname: Right-angled and non-right-angled triangle trigonometry: sine rule, cosine rule, area
text:
![triangle ABC with AB = x cm, AC = (x + 2) cm, BC = 7 cm and angle A = 120 degrees](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.2_12.svg)

In triangle $ABC$, $AB = x\text{ cm}$, $AC = (x + 2)\text{ cm}$, $BC = 7\text{ cm}$ and $B\hat{A}C = 120^\circ$.

(a) Show that $x^2 + 2x - 15 = 0$. [3]

(b) Find the value of $x$. [2]

(c) Find the exact area of triangle $ABC$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$7^2=x^2+(x+2)^2-2x(x+2)\cos120^\circ$ M1

$\cos120^\circ=-\frac{1}{2}$, so $49=x^2+x^2+4x+4+x^2+2x$ A1

$3x^2+6x-45=0$ A1

$x^2+2x-15=0$ AG

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$(x+5)(x-3)=0$ (M1)

$x=3$ (reject $x=-5$ as a length cannot be negative) A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

area $=\frac{1}{2}(3)(5)\sin120^\circ$ (M1)

$=\frac{15\sqrt{3}}{4}\text{ cm}^2$ A1

Note: FT from (b).

**[2 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: Applications of trigonometry: bearings, angles of elevation and depression
text:
![tower TF with points A and B on level ground; angle of elevation 32 degrees from A, 40 m from F; B is 15 m closer](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.3_13.svg)

A vertical tower $[TF]$ stands on horizontal ground. From a point $A$ on the ground, $40\text{ m}$ from the foot $F$, the angle of elevation of the top $T$ is $32^\circ$.

(a) Find the height of the tower. [2]

Ana walks $15\text{ m}$ directly towards the tower from $A$ to the point $B$.

(b) Find $\theta$, the angle of elevation of $T$ from $B$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$\tan32^\circ=\frac{TF}{40}$ (M1)

$TF=25.0\text{ m}$ $(24.9947\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$BF=40-15=25\text{ m}$ (A1)

$\tan\theta=\frac{24.9947\ldots}{25}$ (M1)

$\theta=45.0^\circ$ $(44.9940\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [5 marks]**

tname: Applications of trigonometry: bearings, angles of elevation and depression
text:
![bearings diagram: P to Q is 12 km on bearing 065 degrees, Q to R is 8 km on bearing 150 degrees](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.3_14.svg)

A boat sails $12\text{ km}$ from port $P$ on a bearing of $065^\circ$ to a buoy $Q$. It then sails $8\text{ km}$ on a bearing of $150^\circ$ to a lighthouse $R$.

(a) Show that $P\hat{Q}R = 95^\circ$. [2]

(b) Find the distance $PR$. [2]

(c) Find the bearing of $R$ from $P$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

bearing of $P$ from $Q$ is $065^\circ+180^\circ=245^\circ$ (or angle between north at $Q$ and $QP$ is $65^\circ$ by alternate angles) M1

$P\hat{Q}R=245^\circ-150^\circ$ (or $(180^\circ-150^\circ)+65^\circ$) A1

$=95^\circ$ AG

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$PR^2=12^2+8^2-2(12)(8)\cos95^\circ$ (M1)

$PR=15.0\text{ km}$ $(14.9911\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

$\frac{\sin Q\hat{P}R}{8}=\frac{\sin95^\circ}{14.9911\ldots}$ (M1)

$Q\hat{P}R=32.1^\circ$ $(32.1148\ldots)$ A1

bearing $=065^\circ+32.1^\circ=097.1^\circ$ (accept $097^\circ$) A1

Note: FT from (b).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: Applications of trigonometry: bearings, angles of elevation and depression
text:
![cliff TF of height 85 m with boats at A and B; angles of depression 18 degrees and 27 degrees from T](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.3_15.svg)

From the top $T$ of a vertical cliff $85\text{ m}$ above sea level, the angle of depression of a boat at point $A$ is $18^\circ$. The boat sails directly towards the foot of the cliff, $F$, and stops at point $B$, where the angle of depression from $T$ is $27^\circ$.

(a) Find the distance $AF$. [2]

(b) Find the distance $AB$. [3]

(c) The boat took $40$ seconds to sail from $A$ to $B$. Find its average speed, in $\text{m s}^{-1}$. [1]
ms:
**(a)**

$T\hat{A}F=18^\circ$ (alternate angles), $\tan18^\circ=\frac{85}{AF}$ (M1)

$AF=262\text{ m}$ $(261.603\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$BF=\frac{85}{\tan27^\circ}$ (M1)

$=166.821\ldots$ (A1)

$AB=261.603\ldots-166.821\ldots=94.8\text{ m}$ $(94.7812\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[3 marks]**

**(c)**

$\frac{94.7812\ldots}{40}=2.37\text{ m s}^{-1}$ A1

Note: FT from (b).

**[1 mark]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Applications of trigonometry: bearings, angles of elevation and depression
text:
A hiker walks $10\text{ km}$ from point $A$ on a bearing of $030^\circ$ to point $B$. She then walks $10\sqrt{3}\text{ km}$ on a bearing of $120^\circ$ to point $C$.

(a) Show that $A\hat{B}C = 90^\circ$. [2]

(b) Find the distance $AC$. [2]

(c) Find the bearing of $C$ from $A$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $210^\circ$ (or angle between north at $B$ and $BA$ is $180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ$ measured clockwise) M1

$A\hat{B}C=210^\circ-120^\circ=90^\circ$ A1AG

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$AC^2=10^2+\left(10\sqrt{3}\right)^2=100+300$ (M1)

$AC=20\text{ km}$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

$\tan B\hat{A}C=\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{10}=\sqrt{3}\Rightarrow B\hat{A}C=60^\circ$ (M1)

bearing $=030^\circ+60^\circ=090^\circ$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Applications of trigonometry: bearings, angles of elevation and depression
text:
![plan view: A and B are 200 m apart with B due east of A; the bearing of F from A is 050 degrees and from B is 320 degrees](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.3_17.svg)

Two surveyors stand at points $A$ and $B$ on horizontal ground, where $B$ is $200\text{ m}$ due east of $A$. A vertical mast $[FT]$ has its foot $F$ on the same ground. The bearing of $F$ from $A$ is $050^\circ$ and the bearing of $F$ from $B$ is $320^\circ$. The diagram shows a plan view.

(a) (i) Write down the size of $F\hat{A}B$.

(ii) Show that $A\hat{F}B = 90^\circ$. [3]

(b) Find $AF$. [2]

The angle of elevation of the top of the mast, $T$, from $A$ is $12^\circ$.

(c) Find the height of the mast. [2]

(d) Find the angle of elevation of $T$ from $B$. [3]

(e) The point $M$ is the midpoint of $[AB]$. Find the angle of elevation of $T$ from $M$. [3]
ms:
**(a)(i)**

$F\hat{A}B=90^\circ-50^\circ=40^\circ$ A1

**(a)(ii)**

$A\hat{B}F=320^\circ-270^\circ=50^\circ$ M1A1

$A\hat{F}B=180^\circ-40^\circ-50^\circ=90^\circ$ AG

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$AF=200\cos40^\circ$ (M1)

$=153\text{ m}$ $(153.208\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

$FT=153.208\ldots\times\tan12^\circ$ (M1)

$=32.6\text{ m}$ $(32.5655\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(d)**

$BF=200\sin40^\circ=128.557\ldots$ (A1)

$\tan\alpha=\frac{32.5655\ldots}{128.557\ldots}$ (M1)

$\alpha=14.2^\circ$ $(14.2148\ldots)$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(e)**

$FM=100\text{ m}$ (midpoint of the hypotenuse of right-angled triangle $AFB$ is equidistant from $A$, $B$ and $F$; or cosine rule $FM^2=153.208\ldots^2+100^2-2(153.208\ldots)(100)\cos40^\circ$) (M1)A1

$\tan\beta=\frac{32.5655\ldots}{100}\Rightarrow\beta=18.0^\circ$ $(18.0381\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (c) throughout.

**[3 marks]**

**Total [13 marks]**

tname: The circle: radian measure, arc length and sector area
text:
![sector OAB of radius 6 cm with angle 2 pi over 3](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.4_18.svg)

The diagram shows a sector $OAB$ of a circle with centre $O$ and radius $6\text{ cm}$, where $A\hat{O}B = \frac{2\pi}{3}$.

(a) Find the length of the arc $AB$. [2]

(b) Find the area of the sector $OAB$. [2]

(c) Find the perimeter of the sector $OAB$. [1]
ms:
**(a)**

$l=6\times\frac{2\pi}{3}$ (M1)

$=4\pi\text{ cm}$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$A=\frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)$ (M1)

$=12\pi\text{ cm}^2$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

perimeter $=12+4\pi\text{ cm}$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[1 mark]**

**Total [5 marks]**

tname: The circle: radian measure, arc length and sector area
text:
(a) Express $150^\circ$ in radians. [1]

A sector of a circle of radius $r\text{ cm}$ has an angle of $150^\circ$ at the centre and an area of $15\pi\text{ cm}^2$.

(b) Find the value of $r$. [3]

(c) Find the arc length of the sector, giving your answer in terms of $\pi$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$\frac{5\pi}{6}$ A1

**[1 mark]**

**(b)**

$\frac{1}{2}r^2\left(\frac{5\pi}{6}\right)=15\pi$ M1

$r^2=36$ A1

$r=6$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(c)**

$l=6\times\frac{5\pi}{6}$ (M1)

$=5\pi\text{ cm}$ A1

Note: FT from (b).

**[2 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: The circle: radian measure, arc length and sector area
text:
![circle centre O radius 8 cm with chord AB subtending 1.2 radians; the minor segment is shaded](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.4_20.svg)

The diagram shows a circle with centre $O$ and radius $8\text{ cm}$. The points $A$ and $B$ lie on the circle and $A\hat{O}B = 1.2$ radians. The shaded region is the minor segment bounded by the chord $[AB]$ and the minor arc $AB$.

(a) Find the length of the chord $[AB]$. [2]

(b) Find the area of the shaded segment. [3]

(c) Find the perimeter of the shaded segment. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$AB^2=8^2+8^2-2(8)(8)\cos1.2$ (or $AB=2\times8\sin0.6$) (M1)

$AB=9.03\text{ cm}$ $(9.03427\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

sector area $=\frac{1}{2}(8^2)(1.2)=38.4$; triangle area $=\frac{1}{2}(8^2)\sin1.2=29.8252\ldots$ (A1)(A1)

segment area $=38.4-29.8252\ldots=8.57\text{ cm}^2$ $(8.57474\ldots)$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(c)**

arc $AB=8\times1.2=9.6$ (A1)

perimeter $=9.6+9.03427\ldots=18.6\text{ cm}$ $(18.6342\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[2 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: The circle: radian measure, arc length and sector area
text:
A sector of a circle has radius $r\text{ cm}$ and angle $\theta$ radians at the centre, where $0 < \theta < 2\pi$. The perimeter of the sector is $20\text{ cm}$ and its area is $16\text{ cm}^2$.

(a) Show that $r^2 - 10r + 16 = 0$. [4]

(b) Hence find the value of $r$ and the value of $\theta$, justifying your answer. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$2r+r\theta=20$ A1

$\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta=16$ A1

$r\theta=20-2r\Rightarrow\frac{1}{2}r(20-2r)=16$ M1

$10r-r^2=16$ A1

$r^2-10r+16=0$ AG

**[4 marks]**

**(b)**

$(r-2)(r-8)=0\Rightarrow r=2$ or $r=8$ A1

if $r=2$, $\theta=\frac{20-4}{2}=8$, but $8>2\pi$, so reject R1

$r=8$, $\theta=\frac{20-16}{8}=0.5$ A1

Note: award R1 for a valid reason for rejecting $r=2$ (e.g. $\theta=8>2\pi$ is impossible for a sector).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: The circle: radian measure, arc length and sector area
text:
![two circles of radius 6 cm with centres O1 and O2, 6 cm apart, intersecting at P and Q; the common region is shaded](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.4_22.svg)

Two circles, each of radius $6\text{ cm}$, have centres $O_1$ and $O_2$, where $O_1O_2 = 6\text{ cm}$. The circles intersect at the points $P$ and $Q$. The region common to both circles is shaded.

(a) Show that $P\hat{O}_1Q = \frac{2\pi}{3}$. [3]

(b) Find the length $PQ$. [2]

(c) Find the area of the shaded region. [4]

(d) Find the perimeter of the shaded region. [2]

(e) A single circle has the same area as the shaded region. Find the radius of this circle. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$O_1P=O_2P=O_1O_2=6$, so triangle $O_1O_2P$ is equilateral R1

$P\hat{O}_1O_2=\frac{\pi}{3}$ A1

by symmetry $Q\hat{O}_1O_2=\frac{\pi}{3}$, so $P\hat{O}_1Q=\frac{2\pi}{3}$ R1AG

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$PQ^2=6^2+6^2-2(6)(6)\cos\frac{2\pi}{3}$ (or $PQ=2\times6\sin\frac{\pi}{3}$) (M1)

$PQ=6\sqrt{3}=10.4\text{ cm}$ $(10.3923\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

area of one segment $=$ sector $-$ triangle (M1)

$=\frac{1}{2}(6^2)\left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)-\frac{1}{2}(6^2)\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}=37.6991\ldots-15.5884\ldots$ (A1)

$=22.1106\ldots$ (A1)

shaded area $=2\times22.1106\ldots=44.2\text{ cm}^2$ $(44.2213\ldots)$ A1

**[4 marks]**

**(d)**

perimeter $=2\times6\times\frac{2\pi}{3}$ (M1)

$=8\pi=25.1\text{ cm}$ $(25.1327\ldots)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(e)**

$\pi r^2=44.2213\ldots$ (M1)

$r=3.75\text{ cm}$ $(3.75181\ldots)$ A1

Note: FT from (c).

**[2 marks]**

**Total [13 marks]**

tname: The unit circle and exact values; ambiguous case of the sine rule
text:
Find the exact value of each of the following.

(a) $\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}$ [2]

(b) $\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}$ [2]

(c) $\sin\frac{11\pi}{6}$ [2]
ms:
**(a)**

reference angle $\frac{\pi}{3}$ in the third quadrant, where cosine is negative (M1)

$\cos\frac{4\pi}{3}=-\frac{1}{2}$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

reference angle $\frac{\pi}{4}$ in the second quadrant, where tangent is negative (M1)

$\tan\frac{3\pi}{4}=-1$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

reference angle $\frac{\pi}{6}$ in the fourth quadrant, where sine is negative (M1)

$\sin\frac{11\pi}{6}=-\frac{1}{2}$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: The unit circle and exact values; ambiguous case of the sine rule
text:
![unit circle with point P(-3/5, 4/5) at angle theta from the positive x-axis](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.5_24.svg)

The diagram shows the unit circle with centre $O$. The point $P\left(-\frac{3}{5},\ \frac{4}{5}\right)$ lies on the circle and $\theta$ is the angle between the positive $x$-axis and $[OP]$, measured anticlockwise.

(a) Write down the value of $\cos\theta$. [1]

(b) Find the value of $\tan\theta$. [1]

(c) Find the value of $\sin(\theta + \pi)$. [2]

(d) Find the value of $\cos(\pi - \theta)$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$\cos\theta=-\frac{3}{5}$ A1

**[1 mark]**

**(b)**

$\tan\theta=\frac{4/5}{-3/5}=-\frac{4}{3}$ A1

**[1 mark]**

**(c)**

the point for angle $\theta+\pi$ is $\left(\frac{3}{5},\ -\frac{4}{5}\right)$ (or $\sin(\theta+\pi)=-\sin\theta$) (M1)

$\sin(\theta+\pi)=-\frac{4}{5}$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(d)**

$\cos(\pi-\theta)=-\cos\theta$ (or the point for $\pi-\theta$ is $\left(\frac{3}{5},\ \frac{4}{5}\right)$) (M1)

$=\frac{3}{5}$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[2 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: The unit circle and exact values; ambiguous case of the sine rule
text:
![ambiguous case: B with angle 40 degrees, BA = 12 cm, and two possible positions C1 and C2 with AC = 9 cm](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.5_25.svg)

In triangle $ABC$, $AB = 12\text{ cm}$, $AC = 9\text{ cm}$ and $A\hat{B}C = 40^\circ$. The diagram shows that there are two possible positions, $C_1$ and $C_2$, for the point $C$.

(a) Find the two possible values of $A\hat{C}B$. [4]

(b) Given that $A\hat{C}B$ is obtuse, find $BC$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$\frac{\sin A\hat{C}B}{12}=\frac{\sin40^\circ}{9}$ (M1)

$\sin A\hat{C}B=0.857047\ldots$ (A1)

$A\hat{C}B=59.0^\circ$ $(58.9870\ldots)$ A1

or $A\hat{C}B=180^\circ-58.9870\ldots^\circ=121^\circ$ $(121.013\ldots)$ A1

**[4 marks]**

**(b)**

$B\hat{A}C=180^\circ-40^\circ-121.013\ldots^\circ=18.9870\ldots^\circ$ (A1)

$\frac{BC}{\sin18.9870\ldots^\circ}=\frac{9}{\sin40^\circ}$ (M1)

$BC=4.56\text{ cm}$ $(4.55544\ldots)$ A1

Note: alternatively, the cosine rule $9^2=12^2+BC^2-24\,BC\cos40^\circ$ gives $BC=4.56$ or $13.8$; award (A1)(M1) and A1 for selecting $4.56$.

**[3 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: The unit circle and exact values; ambiguous case of the sine rule
text:
In triangle $ABC$, $A\hat{B}C = \frac{\pi}{6}$, $AB = 10\text{ cm}$ and $AC = x\text{ cm}$.

(a) Find the value of $x$ for which the triangle is right-angled at $C$. [2]

(b) Find the set of values of $x$ for which two non-congruent triangles $ABC$ can be drawn. [3]

(c) Given that $x = 5\sqrt{2}$, find the two possible values of $A\hat{C}B$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$x=10\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$ (M1)

$x=5$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$\sin A\hat{C}B=\frac{10\sin\frac{\pi}{6}}{x}=\frac{5}{x}$; two triangles need $\sin A\hat{C}B<1$, so $x>5$ (M1)

and $AC<AB$ (otherwise the obtuse value of $A\hat{C}B$ makes the angle sum at least $\pi$), so $x<10$ R1

$5<x<10$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**(c)**

$\frac{\sin A\hat{C}B}{10}=\frac{\sin\frac{\pi}{6}}{5\sqrt{2}}\Rightarrow\sin A\hat{C}B=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ M1A1

$A\hat{C}B=\frac{\pi}{4}$ or $\frac{3\pi}{4}$ A1

Note: accept $45^\circ$ and $135^\circ$.

**[3 marks]**

**Total [8 marks]**

tname: The unit circle and exact values; ambiguous case of the sine rule
text:
(a) Show that $2\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}\tan\frac{\pi}{6} = 1$. [3]

(b) Find the exact value of $\cos^2\frac{3\pi}{4} - \sin\frac{7\pi}{6}$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$\sin\frac{2\pi}{3}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ A1

$\tan\frac{\pi}{6}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ A1

$2\times\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=1$ A1AG

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$\cos\frac{3\pi}{4}=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, so $\cos^2\frac{3\pi}{4}=\frac{1}{2}$ A1

$\sin\frac{7\pi}{6}=-\frac{1}{2}$ A1

$\frac{1}{2}-\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)=1$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Pythagorean identity and double angle identities
text:
Let $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$, where $\frac{\pi}{2} < \theta < \pi$.

(a) Find the value of $\cos\theta$. [2]

(b) Find the value of $\sin2\theta$. [2]

(c) Find the value of $\cos2\theta$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$\cos^2\theta=1-\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2=\frac{16}{25}$ (M1)

$\cos\theta=-\frac{4}{5}$ (negative since $\theta$ is in the second quadrant) A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$\sin2\theta=2\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right)$ (M1)

$=-\frac{24}{25}$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

$\cos2\theta=1-2\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)^2$ (or $2\cos^2\theta-1$ or $\cos^2\theta-\sin^2\theta$) (M1)

$=\frac{7}{25}$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Pythagorean identity and double angle identities
text:
(a) Show that $(\sin x + \cos x)^2 = 1 + \sin2x$. [3]

(b) Hence find the exact value of $\sin\frac{\pi}{12} + \cos\frac{\pi}{12}$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$(\sin x+\cos x)^2=\sin^2x+2\sin x\cos x+\cos^2x$ M1

$\sin^2x+\cos^2x=1$ A1

$2\sin x\cos x=\sin2x$ A1

so $(\sin x+\cos x)^2=1+\sin2x$ AG

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$\left(\sin\frac{\pi}{12}+\cos\frac{\pi}{12}\right)^2=1+\sin\frac{\pi}{6}$ (M1)

$=\frac{3}{2}$ A1

$\sin\frac{\pi}{12}+\cos\frac{\pi}{12}>0$, so $\sin\frac{\pi}{12}+\cos\frac{\pi}{12}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}$ A1

Note: the final A1 requires the negative root to be rejected (or the positive root to be justified).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Pythagorean identity and double angle identities
text:
(a) Show that $\frac{1 - \cos2x}{\sin2x} = \tan x$, for $\sin2x \neq 0$. [4]

(b) Hence find the exact value of $\tan\frac{\pi}{8}$, giving your answer in the form $\sqrt{a} - b$, where $a,\ b \in \mathbb{Z}$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$1-\cos2x=1-(1-2\sin^2x)=2\sin^2x$ M1A1

$\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x$ A1

$\frac{2\sin^2x}{2\sin x\cos x}=\frac{\sin x}{\cos x}$ A1

$=\tan x$ AG

**[4 marks]**

**(b)**

$\tan\frac{\pi}{8}=\frac{1-\cos\frac{\pi}{4}}{\sin\frac{\pi}{4}}=\frac{1-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$ M1A1

$=\frac{2-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}}=\sqrt{2}-1$ A1

**[3 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: Pythagorean identity and double angle identities
text:
Let $f(x) = \cos2x + 3\sin x$.

(a) Show that $f(x) - 2 = -(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x - 1)$. [3]

(b) Find the exact maximum value of $f(x)$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$\cos2x=1-2\sin^2x$ M1

$f(x)-2=1-2\sin^2x+3\sin x-2=-2\sin^2x+3\sin x-1$ A1

$=-(2\sin^2x-3\sin x+1)$ A1

$=-(2\sin x-1)(\sin x-1)$ AG

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

$f(x)=-2s^2+3s+1$ where $s=\sin x$, $-1\le s\le1$ (M1)

maximum at $s=\frac{3}{4}$ (vertex, which lies in $[-1,\ 1]$) A1

$f_{\max}=-2\left(\frac{9}{16}\right)+\frac{9}{4}+1=\frac{17}{8}$ A1

Note: an answer of $2$ (from $s=1$ or $s=\frac{1}{2}$) receives no further marks after (M1).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [6 marks]**

tname: Pythagorean identity and double angle identities
text:
Let $f(x) = 8\sin x\cos x\cos2x$, for $0 \le x \le \frac{\pi}{2}$.

(a) Show that $f(x) = 2\sin4x$. [3]

(b) (i) Write down the period of the graph of $y = 2\sin4x$.

(ii) Write down the range of $f$. [3]

(c) Solve $f(x) = 1$. [4]

(d) The equation $f(x) = k$ has exactly one solution. Find the possible values of $k$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$2\sin x\cos x=\sin2x$, so $f(x)=4\sin2x\cos2x$ M1A1

$4\sin2x\cos2x=2(2\sin2x\cos2x)=2\sin4x$ A1AG

**[3 marks]**

**(b)(i)**

period $=\frac{2\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}$ $(1.57)$ A1

**(b)(ii)**

$-2\le f(x)\le2$ A1A1

Note: award A1 for each correct end point with correct inequalities; accept $[-2,\ 2]$.

**[3 marks]**

**(c)**

$\sin4x=\frac{1}{2}$, with $0\le4x\le2\pi$ (M1)

$4x=\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{5\pi}{6}$ (A1)

$x=\frac{\pi}{24}=0.131,\quad x=\frac{5\pi}{24}=0.654$ A1A1

Note: award A0 for the second A1 if extra solutions (e.g. $\frac{13\pi}{24}$) outside the domain are included. Accept answers from a graph on the GDC.

**[4 marks]**

**(d)**

$k=2$ or $k=-2$ A1A1

Note: for $-2<k<2$, $k\ne0$, there are two solutions; for $k=0$ there are three.

**[2 marks]**

**Total [12 marks]**

tname: Circular functions: sin, cos, tan graphs, amplitude, period, transformations
text:
Let $f(x) = 3\sin2x + 1$, for $x \in \mathbb{R}$.

(a) Write down the amplitude of $f$. [1]

(b) Find the period of $f$. [1]

(c) Find the range of $f$. [2]

tname: Circular functions: sin, cos, tan graphs, amplitude, period, transformations
text:
![graph of y = a cos(bx) + d for 0 <= x <= 4 with maxima at (0, 7) and (4, 7) and a minimum at (2, -1)](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.7_34.svg)

The graph of $f(x) = a\cos(bx) + d$, for $0 \le x \le 4$, is shown above. The graph has maximum points at $(0,\ 7)$ and $(4,\ 7)$ and a minimum point at $(2,\ -1)$.

(a) Find the value of $a$. [2]

(b) Find the value of $d$. [1]

(c) Find the value of $b$. [2]

(d) Solve $f(x) = 5$ for $0 \le x \le 4$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$a=\frac{7-(-1)}{2}$ (M1)

$a=4$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(b)**

$d=\frac{7+(-1)}{2}=3$ A1

**[1 mark]**

**(c)**

period $=4$ (A1)

$b=\frac{2\pi}{4}=\frac{\pi}{2}$ $(1.57)$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(d)**

$4\cos\left(\frac{\pi x}{2}\right)+3=5$ (or a sketch of $y=5$ intersecting the graph) (M1)

$x=0.667\ \left(\frac{2}{3}\right),\quad x=3.33\ \left(\frac{10}{3}\right)$ A1

Note: FT from their values of $a$, $b$ and $d$.

**[2 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: Circular functions: sin, cos, tan graphs, amplitude, period, transformations
text:
The height, $h$ metres, of a seat on a Ferris wheel above the ground is modelled by
$$h(t) = 25 - 23\cos\left(\frac{\pi t}{10}\right),$$
where $t$ is the time in minutes after the seat passes its lowest point, $t \ge 0$.

(a) (i) Write down the minimum height of the seat.

(ii) Write down the maximum height of the seat. [2]

(b) Find the time taken for the wheel to complete one full revolution. [1]

(c) Find the height of the seat when $t = 4$. [2]

(d) During one revolution, find the length of time for which the seat is more than $40$ metres above the ground. [3]

tname: Circular functions: sin, cos, tan graphs, amplitude, period, transformations
text:
The graph of $y = \sin x$ is transformed onto the graph of $y = g(x)$ by the following sequence of transformations:

- a horizontal translation of $\frac{\pi}{4}$ units to the right, then
- a vertical stretch with scale factor $2$, then
- a vertical translation of $1$ unit down.

(a) Write down an expression for $g(x)$. [3]

(b) Find the range of $g$. [2]

(c) Find the exact value of $g(0)$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$g(x)=2\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-1$ A1A1A1

Note: award A1 for $\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)$, A1 for the factor $2$, A1 for $-1$. Award A1A1A0 for $2\left(\sin\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-1\right)$.

**[3 marks]**

**(b)**

maximum $2-1=1$, minimum $-2-1=-3$ (A1)

$-3\le g(x)\le1$ A1

Note: FT from (a).

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

$g(0)=2\sin\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)-1=2\left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)-1$ (M1)

$=-\sqrt{2}-1$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: Circular functions: sin, cos, tan graphs, amplitude, period, transformations
text:
Let $f(x) = 2\cos2x + 1$, for $0 \le x \le \pi$.

(a) Write down the period of $f$. [1]

(b) Find the range of $f$. [2]

(c) Solve $f(x) = 0$. [4]

(d) Sketch the graph of $y = f(x)$, showing the coordinates of any maximum and minimum points and the $x$-intercepts. [3]

The function $g$ is obtained by translating the graph of $f$ by $\frac{\pi}{4}$ units in the positive $x$-direction.

(e) Show that $g(x) = 2\sin2x + 1$. [2]
ms:
**(a)**

$\pi$ A1

**[1 mark]**

**(b)**

maximum $3$, minimum $-1$ (A1)

$-1\le f(x)\le3$ A1

**[2 marks]**

**(c)**

$\cos2x=-\frac{1}{2}$ (A1)

$0\le2x\le2\pi$ (M1)

$2x=\frac{2\pi}{3},\ \frac{4\pi}{3}$ (A1)

$x=\frac{\pi}{3},\ \frac{2\pi}{3}$ A1

**[4 marks]**

**(d)**

![expected sketch of y = 2cos2x + 1 on 0 to pi](qbank/img/gen_math_SL3.7_37.svg)

A1 for correct shape (one full cycle of a cosine curve over $[0,\ \pi]$, endpoints included)

A1 for maximum points $(0,\ 3)$ and $(\pi,\ 3)$ and minimum point $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},\ -1\right)$

A1 for $x$-intercepts at $\frac{\pi}{3}$ and $\frac{2\pi}{3}$

Note: FT from (c) for the intercepts.

**[3 marks]**

**(e)**

$g(x)=f\left(x-\frac{\pi}{4}\right)=2\cos\left(2x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)+1$ M1

$\cos\left(2x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\sin2x$ (e.g. since $\cos\left(\theta-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=\sin\theta$) R1

$g(x)=2\sin2x+1$ AG

**[2 marks]**

**Total [12 marks]**

tname: Solving trigonometric equations in a finite interval
text: Solve the equation $2\sin x = \sqrt{3}$, for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. [4]
ms:
$\sin x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ A1

$x=\frac{\pi}{3}$ A1

recognizing a second solution in the second quadrant, $x=\pi-\frac{\pi}{3}$ (M1)

$x=\frac{2\pi}{3}$ A1

Note: award A0 for the final mark if any additional solutions are given.

**Total [4 marks]**

tname: Solving trigonometric equations in a finite interval
text: Solve the equation $2\cos^2x + 3\sin x - 3 = 0$, for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. [7]
ms:
$2(1-\sin^2x)+3\sin x-3=0$ M1

$2\sin^2x-3\sin x+1=0$ A1

$(2\sin x-1)(\sin x-1)=0$ M1

$\sin x=\frac{1}{2}$ A1

$\sin x=1$ A1

$x=\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{5\pi}{6}$ A1

$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$ A1

Note: award the final two A1 marks only if no additional solutions are given.

**Total [7 marks]**

tname: Solving trigonometric equations in a finite interval
text: Solve the equation $\tan2x = \sqrt{3}$, for $-\pi \le x \le \pi$. [5]
ms:
$2x=\frac{\pi}{3}$ (A1)

$-2\pi\le2x\le2\pi$ and the period of $\tan$ is $\pi$: $2x=\frac{\pi}{3}+k\pi$ (M1)

$2x=-\frac{5\pi}{3},\ -\frac{2\pi}{3},\ \frac{\pi}{3},\ \frac{4\pi}{3}$ A1

$x=-\frac{5\pi}{6},\ -\frac{\pi}{3},\ \frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{2\pi}{3}$ A2

Note: award A1 for two or three correct values of $x$ and no incorrect values; A2 for all four and no others.

**Total [5 marks]**

tname: Solving trigonometric equations in a finite interval
text: Solve the equation $3\cos2x = 2\sin x$, for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. [6]
ms:
**METHOD 1**

$3(1-2\sin^2x)=2\sin x$ M1

$6\sin^2x+2\sin x-3=0$ A1

$\sin x=\frac{-2\pm\sqrt{76}}{12}$, so $\sin x=0.559816\ldots$ or $\sin x=-0.893149\ldots$ (M1)A1

$x=0.594,\ 2.55$ A1

$x=4.25,\ 5.18$ A1

**METHOD 2**

graph $y=3\cos2x$ and $y=2\sin x$ (or $y=3\cos2x-2\sin x$) on $0\le x\le2\pi$ (M1)

award A1 for each correct solution, up to A4, and the final A1 for exactly four solutions with no extras

**Total [6 marks]**

Note: answers are $0.594163\ldots,\ 2.54742\ldots,\ 4.24589\ldots,\ 5.17888\ldots$

tname: Solving trigonometric equations in a finite interval
text: Solve the equation $3\tan^2x - 5\tan x - 2 = 0$, for $0 \le x \le \pi$, $x \neq \frac{\pi}{2}$. [5]
ms:
$(3\tan x+1)(\tan x-2)=0$ (or quadratic formula, or GDC) M1

$\tan x=2$ or $\tan x=-\frac{1}{3}$ A1

$x=1.11$ $(1.10714\ldots)$ A1

recognizing that $\tan x<0$ gives an angle in the second quadrant: $x=\pi-\arctan\frac{1}{3}$ (M1)

$x=2.82$ $(2.81984\ldots)$ A1

Note: award A0 for $x=-0.322$ as it is outside the domain.

**Total [5 marks]**

tname: Solving trigonometric equations in a finite interval
text:
(a) Solve the equation $\sin2x = \cos x$, for $0 \le x \le 2\pi$. [5]

(b) Hence solve the equation $\sin4x = \cos2x$, for $0 \le x \le \pi$. [3]
ms:
**(a)**

$2\sin x\cos x-\cos x=0$ M1

$\cos x(2\sin x-1)=0$ A1

Note: award M0 if both sides are divided by $\cos x$ (losing solutions), but the subsequent A1 for $\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{5\pi}{6}$ may be awarded.

$\cos x=0\Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{2},\ \frac{3\pi}{2}$ A1

$\sin x=\frac{1}{2}\Rightarrow x=\frac{\pi}{6}$ A1

$x=\frac{5\pi}{6}$ A1

**[5 marks]**

**(b)**

let $u=2x$, then $\sin2u=\cos u$ with $0\le u\le2\pi$ (M1)

$u=\frac{\pi}{6},\ \frac{\pi}{2},\ \frac{5\pi}{6},\ \frac{3\pi}{2}$

$x=\frac{\pi}{12},\ \frac{\pi}{4},\ \frac{5\pi}{12},\ \frac{3\pi}{4}$ A2

Note: award A1 for two or three correct values and no incorrect values. FT from (a).

**[3 marks]**

**Total [8 marks]**
